# uapi_firewall_nat (Data Source)

Look up the firewall NAT rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "uapi_firewall_nat" "example" {
  id = "<id>"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Resource id to look up.

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the entry is active.
- `etag` (String) Opaque ETag of the resource's current state.
- `managed` (Boolean) Whether the underlying uci section is uapi-managed.
- `match` (Attributes) Match conditions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match))
- `name` (String) Human-readable label for this NAT rule.
- `snat_ip` (String) IPv4 address to rewrite the source to. Requires target SNAT.
- `snat_port` (String) Port or port range to rewrite the source port to. Requires target SNAT.
- `target` (String) What to do with matched traffic: `SNAT` rewrites the source to `snat_ip`/`snat_port`, `MASQUERADE` rewrites it to the outbound interface address, `ACCEPT` exempts it from source NAT. Defaults to `MASQUERADE`.

<a id="nestedatt--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match`

Read-Only:

- `dest_ip` (String) Destination address to match, in the same forms as `src_ip`.
- `dest_port` (String) Destination port or range to match. Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `device` (String) Outbound interface name to match.
- `family` (String) Address family: any, ipv4, or ipv6. Unset means IPv4 only, firewall4's backwards-compatible default for NAT; set `any` for dual-stack.
- `mark` (String) Match an fwmark as a value or value/mask, decimal or `0x` hex. Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `proto` (List of String) Protocols to match, by name or number (`tcp`, `udp`, `gre`, `sctp`, `47`) or a wildcard (`all`, `any`, `tcpudp`). Every protocol must be tcp or udp when a port is matched, because firewall4 keeps a port match only on those. Defaults to all when unset.
- `src_ip` (String) Source address to match: an address, a prefix in either family, or a uci network name. Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `src_port` (String) Source port or range to match. Prefix with `!` to negate.
- `src_zone` (String) Outbound (postrouting) zone this rule applies to. Unset matches all egress traffic.
